tool_args.old_string: To assess task generalization, we evaluate both models on GSM8K at $s \in \{0.25, 0.30\}$. On DeepSeek (clean data, no output truncation), the phase gradient direction is consistent with MATH-500: importance-based eviction concentrates II in the low-sparsity phase while random eviction shows uniformly elevated II. However, strategy specificity exhibits \emph{task-modulated attenuation}: the importance/random gradient ratio decreases from $15$--$17{\times}$ (MATH-500) to $1.1$--$2.2{\times}$ (GSM8K; DeepSeek $s{=}0.30$: $2.1{\times}$). We attribute this attenuation to \emph{task complexity}: GSM8K's simpler arithmetic reasoning induces more uniform attention distributions across phases, yielding a flatter sparsity landscape that reduces sensitivity to eviction strategy choice. Supporting this interpretation, within MATH-500 longer traces---which correlate with harder problems---exhibit significantly higher strategy specificity (Spearman $\rho > 0$, $p < 0.02$), consistent with cognitive load as the modulating variable. Qwen confirms directional consistency ($s{=}0.25$: $1.6{\times}$); however, Qwen outputs were truncated at \texttt{max\_new\_tokens}${=}$2047 across all GSM8K problems, so absolute values should be interpreted with this limitation. Full tables in Appendix~\ref{app:gsm8k}.

tool_args.old_string: To assess task generalization, we evaluate both models on GSM8K at $s \in \{0.25, 0.30\}$. On DeepSeek (clean data, no output truncation), the phase gradient direction is consistent with MATH-500: importance-based eviction concentrates II in the low-sparsity phase while random eviction shows uniformly elevated II. Crucially, strategy specificity on GSM8K manifests as a \emph{qualitative} gap rather than a quantitative ratio: importance-based eviction produces significant phase gradients while random eviction is non-significant across all GSM8K conditions (CIs spanning zero), precluding meaningful ratio computation. This qualitative separation---significant vs.\ non-significant---provides complementary evidence for strategy specificity beyond the quantitative $15$--$17{\times}$ ratio observed on MATH-500. We attribute the shift from quantitative to qualitative contrast to \emph{task complexity}: GSM8K's simpler arithmetic reasoning induces more uniform attention distributions across phases, yielding a flatter sparsity landscape where random eviction's phase gradient vanishes entirely. Supporting this interpretation, within MATH-500 longer traces---which correlate with harder problems---exhibit significantly higher strategy specificity (Spearman $\rho > 0$, $p < 0.02$), consistent with cognitive load as the modulating variable. Qwen confirms directional consistency ($s{=}0.25$: importance significant, random non-significant); however, Qwen outputs were truncated at \texttt{max\_new\_tokens}${=}$2047 across all GSM8K problems, so absolute values should be interpreted with this limitation.
